lore_anchors.definition: A person used as a cultivation vessel; their essence and cultivation are forcibly extracted by a higher-level cultivator for personal advancement. It is a brutal, institutionalized form of exploitation in the xianxia world, stripping the victim of agency and treating them as a consumable resource.

A dangerous frontier island in the Outer Star Seas, known for its self-sufficient resources and brutal living conditions. It serves as a haven for factions and cultivators seeking to escape the direct control of the Inner Star Seas, but at a high cost.
A fourth-grade earth-attribute demon beast known for its steel-like feathers and incredible flight speed. Its eggs are a valuable commodity in the Outer Star Seas.

The dangerous, outer boundary of the cultivation world, reaching toward the chaotic regions beyond. It is a frontier of high risk and high reward, where the established rules of more civilized regions are bent or broken.

The second major stage of cultivation in RMJI. A cultivator’s body and spirit are fundamentally restructured, granting greatly extended lifespan (around 200 years) and the ability to wield true magic tools. It marks the transition from a mere mortal to a true player in the cultivation world.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Han Li startled but not outraged by the Human Furnace auction?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Han Li is the ultimate pragmatist in the Mortal Stream. He recognizes the horror of the system, but understands that moral outrage is a luxury that impedes survival. His shock is processed as data, not as a call to action. He files away the information and moves on, calculating the world as it is, not as he wishes it to be.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How does the power of a "Human Furnace" work?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The exact mechanics vary, but it generally involves a higher-level cultivator using a secret technique to drain the life force, spiritual energy, or yin essence from a lower-level cultivator (usually female) during dual cultivation. This artificially boosts the user's cultivation or heals their injuries, while the victim is left weakened, crippled, or dead. The term "furnace" implies a consumable resource.

cultural_notes_faq.q: The auction scene feels very long. Is it just filler?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Absolutely not. This is a crucial "quiet worldbuilding" chapter that defines the unique socio-economic ecosystem of the Outer Star Seas. It demonstrates the Dark Forest principle at an institutional level, showing how scarcity and survival can normalize horrific practices. It also sets the stage for the group’s future decisions and highlights the vast, impersonal cruelty of this new environment.
